claims.statement: The revised Waste Framework Directive requires Member States to establish textile and footwear EPR schemes under common EU rules.
Textile apparel is a priority ESPR product group, with a planned delegated act and product-specific DPP requirements, but the final requirements are not yet fixed.
Demand hypothesis: fibre recyclers will reserve homogeneous factory scrap when composition and forward yield are reliable.

contrary_evidence: Textile DPP obligations depend on a future delegated act and timeline changes are possible.
Mixed-fibre scrap and cheap virgin fibre can undermine recycling economics.

economics.acquisition_route: Demand hypothesis: one recycler's accepted-spec list can be used to recruit a concentrated set of factories
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 40m PLN annual GMV at 4% plus 200 facilities at 1500 PLN monthly yields 5.2m PLN revenue; 25% EBITDA at a 4x value could exceed 5m PLN in 4-6 years
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours weekly for one fibre category and one regional cluster
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 70-82% excluding testing and freight passed through to participants
economics.payback: Economics hypothesis: 30 facilities at 1500 PLN monthly recover setup capital in 12-15 months before transaction revenue
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 1000-3000 PLN monthly per facility plus 3-5% of material GMV
economics.retention_or_repeat: Production generates weekly lots; EPR reporting, composition changes, and forward recycler reservations recur

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Factory-specific composition and yield history, recycler acceptance data, and aggregated forward supply by fibre
fingerprint.customer: Textile and footwear manufacturers, brands, producer-responsibility organizations, sorters, and fibre recyclers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Polish garment clusters, ERP partners, textile labs, producer-responsibility organizations, and recycler partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner authorization, composition evidence, status and condition record, forward yield forecast, recycler specification matching, and EPR/DPP export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Producer pays per facility or brand monthly; seller and buyer pay a transaction fee on reserved volume
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A producer faces textile EPR and future DPP work while recyclers lack predictable, composition-known feedstock

founder_fit: Supply-chain data problem suited to AI
Cluster-based B2B selling limits networking burden

structure.commercial_archetype: Provenance SaaS plus recoverable-material capacity pool
structure.control_point: Authorized recurring factory output and its trusted composition history
structure.critical_dependency: Enough homogeneous material must clear logistics and processing economics; DPP details remain subject to future rules

thesis: Cut-and-sew factories and brands authorize recurring scrap or deadstock lots with composition, origin, condition, and waste status; recyclers reserve future homogeneous volumes and producers reuse the evidence for EPR and DPP readiness. Demand hypothesis: mill-specific yield history is a stronger moat than a generic textile marketplace.
title: Textile Scrap Provenance and Forward-Volume Pool
